All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. title: The Productivity Claims Seminar
instructions: 阅读下面的模拟教育材料（非官方雅思测试，也不代表任何真实研究）。先通读文章，理解研讨会中不同发言者如何转述和评价关于生产力的说法，并注意 some / most / all 的范围差异。然后完成 10 道阅读题：单选题、填空题（答案必须逐字来自原文，且不超过字数限制）和 True/False/Not Given 题。之后学习语法框中的转述动词与限定词规则，并完成 8 道新句子的语法题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。
passage:
A. Last Thursday, the university's Media and Evidence Society held a seminar titled 'Productivity Claims: Who Says So?' About forty students attended. The chair, Dr. Lena Ortiz, opened by saying that the group would examine three widely shared claims about productivity and ask what evidence supported each one. She reminded everyone that a claim is not a fact simply because many people repeat it.

B. The first speaker, Marco Li, presented a claim from a popular blog: 'Working in short bursts makes everyone more productive.' Marco reported that the blog had surveyed its readers and that most respondents said they preferred short work sessions. He then noted a problem. The blog's readers were mostly people who already liked short sessions, so the survey could not speak for all workers. Dr. Ortiz asked whether the blog had measured productivity at all. Marco admitted that it had measured only preference, not output. The seminar agreed that the claim was interesting but not yet supported.

C. The second speaker, Priya Nair, discussed a different claim: 'Some meetings are a waste of time.' She explained that this statement is easier to defend because it uses 'some' rather than 'all'. Her team had observed twelve meetings in one department and found that three of them had no clear agenda and no written decisions. Priya cautioned that twelve meetings in one department cannot represent most workplaces. She said the evidence supported a limited conclusion: some meetings in that department were poorly organized. She did not claim that all meetings are useless.

D. The third speaker, Tom Becker, examined a claim about tools: 'Most productivity apps improve focus.' He described a small trial in which twenty volunteers used a timer app for two weeks. Fourteen said they felt more focused, but only six had completed the daily tasks the researchers set. Tom pointed out that feeling focused and being productive are not the same thing. He also noted that the volunteers had chosen to join the trial, so they may have been unusually motivated. Dr. Ortiz summarized: the trial suggested that some users felt more focused, but it did not show that most apps improve focus for most people.

E. In the final discussion, the chair introduced a checklist for evaluating claims. First, identify the exact words: does the claim say some, most, or all? Second, ask who was studied and how many people were included. Third, separate what people feel from what they produce. Fourth, check whether the original source measured the thing it claims to measure. Several students said the checklist made them notice how often 'most' appears in headlines without numbers behind it. One student, Chen Wei, remarked that he had shared the timer-app claim online before the seminar and now planned to add a correction.

F. The seminar ended with a short writing task. Each student rewrote one claim using a more careful verb and a narrower quantifier. Marco changed his sentence to 'The blog reported that some readers preferred short sessions.' Priya wrote 'The observation suggested that some meetings in one department lacked clear agendas.' Tom wrote 'The trial indicated that some volunteers felt more focused.' Dr. Ortiz closed by saying that careful reporting does not make a claim boring; it makes it honest.

questions.prompt: What did Dr. Lena Ortiz say at the start of the seminar?
options: The group would examine three widely shared claims about productivity.
The group would write a blog about short work sessions.
The group would interview forty workers.
The group would test a new timer app.
answers: The group would examine three widely shared claims about productivity.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: Priya's team observed twelve meetings and found that three of them had no clear ______ and no written decisions.
questions.explanation: 原文第三段说十二次会议中有三次没有明确议程（agenda）和书面决定。答案逐字来自原文。

questions.prompt: What did Priya caution about her evidence?
options: Twelve meetings in one department cannot represent most workplaces.
All meetings are useless.

answers: Twelve meetings in one department cannot represent most workplaces.

Fourteen
Twenty
Twelve

options: They are not the same thing.
They are always the same thing.
Feeling focused is more important than being productive.

answers: They are not the same thing.

questions.prompt: According to the chair's checklist, what should you do first when evaluating a claim?
options: Identify the exact words: some, most, or all.
Ask how many people were included.
Separate feelings from output.
Check the original source's measurement.
answers: Identify the exact words: some, most, or all.
questions.explanation: 原文第五段列出检查清单，第一步是识别确切用词：some、most 还是 all。其他选项是后续步骤。
questions.evidence: First, identify the exact words: does the claim say some, most, or all?

options: Add a correction to a claim he had shared online.
Write a new blog about short sessions.
Join Tom's timer-app trial.

answers: Add a correction to a claim he had shared online.

questions.evidence: he had shared the timer-app claim online before the seminar and now planned to add a correction

False
Not Given

grammar.title: 转述动词、引述与改写、限定词 some / most / all 的范围
grammar.explanation: 当我们转述别人的话时，常用转述动词（reporting verbs），如 say、report、explain、caution、point out、indicate、suggest。这些动词后面常接 that 从句，用来引述或改写原话。例如原文说 'The blog reported that some readers preferred short sessions.' 这里 reported 是转述动词，that 从句是改写后的内容。注意：转述时不要夸大原话的范围。限定词 some（一些）、most（大多数）、all（全部）表示不同的数量范围。some 只指一部分，most 指超过一半但并非全部，all 指全部。原文中 Priya 说 'some meetings' 而不是 'all meetings'，因为证据只支持一部分。转述时如果原话是 some，就不能改成 all 或 most，否则会歪曲证据。请判断下面新句子中转述动词和限定词的使用是否正确。
grammar.example: The trial indicated that some volunteers felt more focused.

questions.prompt: Choose the best reporting verb: The researcher ______ that the survey had measured only preference, not output.
options: admitted
celebrated
refused
forgot
questions.explanation: admitted（承认）适合转述一个不太有利的事实：调查只测量了偏好而非产出。celebrated 表示庆祝，refused 表示拒绝，forgot 表示忘记，都不符合语境。
questions.evidence: Marco admitted that it had measured only preference, not output.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly reports a claim that used 'some'?
options: She reported that some meetings lacked clear agendas.
She reported that all meetings lacked clear agendas.
She reported that most meetings lacked clear agendas.
She reported that no meetings lacked clear agendas.
answers: She reported that some meetings lacked clear agendas.
questions.explanation: 原话只支持一部分会议，因此转述时应保留 some，不能改成 all、most 或 no。
questions.evidence: The observation suggested that some meetings in one department lacked clear agendas.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct quantifier: The team observed twelve meetings, but ______ of them had no clear agenda.
options: three
all
most
every
questions.explanation: 原文说十二次会议中有三次没有明确议程。all、most、every 都夸大了范围，与证据不符。
questions.evidence: three of them had no clear agenda and no written decisions

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a reporting verb correctly?
options: Tom pointed out that feeling focused and being productive are not the same thing.
Tom pointed out that feeling focused and being productive is not the same thing.
Tom pointed out feeling focused and being productive are not the same thing.
Tom pointed out that feeling focused and being productive were not the same thing.
answers: Tom pointed out that feeling focused and being productive are not the same thing.
questions.explanation: point out 后接 that 从句；主语 feeling focused and being productive 是复数概念，用 are。选项 B 主谓不一致，选项 C 缺少 that，选项 D 时态与原文不符。
questions.evidence: Tom pointed out that feeling focused and being productive are not the same thing.

questions.prompt: Choose the best reporting verb: The chair ______ that the group would examine three claims.
options: announced
denied
doubted
prevented
questions.explanation: announced（宣布）适合转述主席开场时的正式说明。denied 表示否认，doubted 表示怀疑，prevented 表示阻止，均不符合。
questions.evidence: the chair, Dr. Lena Ortiz, opened by saying that the group would examine three widely shared claims

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly narrows the claim?
options: The trial indicated that some volunteers felt more focused.
The trial indicated that all volunteers felt more focused.
The trial indicated that most volunteers felt more focused.
The trial indicated that every volunteer felt more focused.
answers: The trial indicated that some volunteers felt more focused.
questions.explanation: 原文只说一些志愿者感觉更专注，因此转述时保留 some 才准确。all、most、every 都扩大了范围。
questions.evidence: The trial indicated that some volunteers felt more focused.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The blog's readers were mostly people who already liked short sessions, so the survey could not speak for ______ workers.
options: all
some
a few
several
questions.explanation: 原文说调查不能代表所有工作者（all workers）。some、a few、several 都只指一部分，不能表达“全部”的意思。
questions.evidence: the survey could not speak for all workers

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses 'most' correctly according to the passage?
options: The blog reported that most respondents preferred short work sessions.
The blog reported that all respondents preferred short work sessions.
The blog reported that some respondents preferred short work sessions.
The blog reported that no respondents preferred short work sessions.
answers: The blog reported that most respondents preferred short work sessions.
questions.explanation: 原文说大多数受访者（most respondents）表示偏好短时段工作。all、some、no 都改变了原话的数量范围。
questions.evidence: most respondents said they preferred short work sessions
